title: Canonical biduality for coherent modules without punctual torsion on a reduced curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $C$ be a nonempty proper reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Choose its dualizing module $\omega_C$ with the natural representing isomorphisms of [lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module]. Let $F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_C$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Assume that for every open subset $U\subseteq C$, a section of $F(U)$ whose germ is zero at every irreducible-component generic point lying in $U$ is zero [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Define $F^\dagger=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_C}(F,\omega_C)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Then $F^\dagger$ is coherent and has the same property of detection of local sections at component generic points. The canonical evaluation morphism
$$\delta_F:F\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_C}(F^\dagger,\omega_C),\qquad \delta_F(f)(\varphi)=\varphi(f)$$
is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_C$-modules. The formula is on every open subset and determines the morphism uniquely. No local freeness, constant generic rank, connectedness, nodal or Gorenstein hypothesis is imposed on $F$ or $C$; the zero module is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0B5A (lemma-local-CM), final assertion and proof: canonical duality on finite Cohen–Macaulay modules. Sheaf form on a reduced pure-dimensional-one curve, whose dualizing module is supplied by lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module; the generic-section condition spells out absence of dimension-zero torsion.

proof.text: Properness includes finite type, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. Every local ring $A$ has dimension at most one: by [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization], chains of its primes give chains in an affine open of $C$. Reducedness and [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-reduced] give $\operatorname{depth}A\geq\min(1,\dim A)=\dim A$; [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension], applied to $A$ as its own module, gives equality. At a closed point $x$ the local dimension is one: dimension zero would make $x$ a component-generic point, whose being closed would give a zero-dimensional component, contrary to pure dimension one. Conversely every nongeneric point is closed, since a further strict specialization would give a chain of length two after adjoining a component-generic point. By [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], every coherent module used below is quasi-coherent of finite type on this locally Noetherian scheme.

source.place: Tags 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), 0BS3 (lemma-duality-dim-1-CM); reduced dimension-one verification as in Tag 0E33.

proof.text: Write $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. It is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field]. On affine charts its finite-type algebras are finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]; properness supplies quasi-compactness and separatedness. Thus [lem-sfb-proper-flat-dualizing-polynomial-model] supplies the right adjoint $f^!$ of $Rf_*$ on quasi-coherent derived categories. Put $K=f^!k[0]$. By [lem-sfb-proper-field-algebraic-dualizing], $K$ has bounded coherent cohomology and each stalk is an algebraic dualizing complex. At each closed point $x$, [lem-sfb-proper-dualizing-closed-stalk-normalized] gives the residue-field normalization of $K_x$.

source.place: Tag 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), construction and normalization in its proof.

proof.text: At a closed point $x$, Step 1 gives a Cohen--Macaulay local ring of dimension one. Apply [lem-sfb-normalized-cm-local-dualizing-concentration] to the normalized $K_x$: it is $H^{-1}(K_x)[1]$, and $H^{-1}(K_x)$ has depth one. Exactness of stalks [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] commutes with kernels and cokernels of the differentials, so $H^j(K)_x=0$ for $j\ne-1$. Each coherent $H^j(K)$ has closed support by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. Schemes are Kolmogorov by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]: points with the same closure would be two generic points of that irreducible closed subset. Since $C$ is quasi-compact, [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point] would put a closed point in any nonempty support. Hence $H^j(K)=0$ for $j\ne-1$. Set $W=H^{-1}(K)$; [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] gives $K\cong W[1]$. In particular $W_x$ has depth one at every closed point.

For every coherent $G$, the degree-zero embedding [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], the adjunction of Step 2, and [lem-trf-field-complex-cohomology-splitting] give natural $k$-linear bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(G,W)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(C)}(G[1],K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(k)}(R\Gamma(C,G)[1],k[0])=\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^1(C,G),k).$$
The last map takes the degree-zero cohomology map; $H^0(R\Gamma(G)[1])=H^1(C,G)$. Thus $W$ with these bijections is a representing pair of [lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module]. Its uniqueness assertion identifies it with the chosen $\omega_C$, respecting the representing bijections. Consequently $K\cong\omega_C[1]$, and at each closed $x$, $K_x\cong(\omega_C)_x[1]$ is normalized and $(\omega_C)_x$ has depth one. This obtains the local dualizing properties from statements of cited nodes, rather than assuming that the representing property alone states those properties.

source.place: Tags 0BS2(5) and 0BS3(3), with the representing-pair uniqueness in 0BS2.

proof.text: The sheaf $F^\dagger=\mathcal Hom(F,\omega_C)$ is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-sheaf-hom-coherent]; applying it again makes $F^{\dagger\dagger}$ coherent. By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-local-finite-presentation], both $F$ and $F^\dagger$ are locally finitely presented, so [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-internal-hom-finite-presentation] gives their Hom stalks as ordinary Hom modules. The comparison sends the germ of a local morphism to its stalk map, a normalization used below. For coherent $G$, [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-affine-sections-finite] gives finite affine section modules, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] identifies $G_x$ with the localization of those modules.

Take an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq C$ and $M=F(V)$. The hypothesis and the stalk/localization dictionary of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] say that $M\to\prod_{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Min}R}M_{\mathfrak q}$ is injective. If $\mathfrak p=\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)$ is an associated prime of $M$ which is not minimal, then for each minimal $\mathfrak q$ choose $a\in\mathfrak p\setminus\mathfrak q$ (otherwise $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$ would force equality by minimality). Since $az=0$, $z/1=0$ in $M_{\mathfrak q}$. Injectivity forces $z=0$, contradicting that its annihilator is a proper prime. Thus every associated prime of $M$ is minimal.

source.place: Tag 0311 (lemma-zero-at-ass-zero), associated-prime criterion; forward implication written out on annihilators.

proof.text: Fix a closed point $x\in V$ with $F_x\ne0$, corresponding to $\mathfrak p\subset R$. This prime is not minimal by Step 1 and is finitely generated since $R$ is Noetherian. If the maximal ideal of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ were the annihilator of an element of $M_{\mathfrak p}$, [lem-sc-associated-localization-fg] would make $\mathfrak p$ associated to $M$, contradicting Step 6. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nonzerodivisor-if-maximal-not-associated] to obtain an injective multiplication $t:F_x\to F_x$ with $t\in\mathfrak m_x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson], $F_x/tF_x\ne0$, since $F_x$ is finite and nonzero and $(t)\subseteq\mathfrak m_x=\operatorname{Jac}(R_{\mathfrak p})$. Thus $t$ is a regular sequence of length one, so depth is at least one by [def-weil-pbc-depth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension], depth is at most the support dimension, which is at most $\dim R_{\mathfrak p}=1$. Therefore $\operatorname{depth}F_x=1$. No depth assertion for a nonzero module was applied to a zero stalk.

source.place: Tag 0B5A (lemma-local-CM), dimension-one Cohen--Macaulay hypothesis; algebra.tex Tags 058A, 00LL and 00LK.

proof.text: The sheaf $\omega_C$ detects sections at component-generic points even on arbitrary opens. Indeed, on an affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, put $P=\omega_C(V)$. If $\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)=\mathfrak p$ is nonminimal and prime, then $z/1\ne0$ in $P_{\mathfrak p}$: an element outside $\mathfrak p$ cannot kill $z$. Its annihilator there is the maximal ideal. By Step 1 this is a closed point of $C$, so Step 4 gives depth one; a length-one regular element of its maximal ideal cannot kill a nonzero element annihilated by that ideal. This contradiction shows $\operatorname{Ass}(P)\subseteq\operatorname{Min}R$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-module-injects-localizations-associated-primes] makes any element vanishing at all minimal primes zero. The affine-section and stalk identifications are [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-affine-sections-finite, lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. Applying this on affine subopens of any open $U$ proves the asserted detection there by the sheaf separation axiom.

source.place: Tag 0311 (lemma-zero-at-ass-zero), with the depth-one exclusion of nongeneric associated primes.

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq C$ and $\varphi\in F^\dagger(U)$ have zero component-generic germs. By [def-pur-sheaf-hom], this is a morphism $F|_U\to\omega_C|_U$. On each open $T\subseteq U$ and $s\in F(T)$, its value $\varphi_T(s)\in\omega_C(T)$ has zero component-generic germs: by the Hom stalk normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-internal-hom-finite-presentation], the germ is $\varphi_\eta(s_\eta)=0$. Step 8 gives $\varphi_T(s)=0$. This holds for every $T,s$, so $\varphi=0$. Thus $F^\dagger$ has precisely the detection property required in the statement.

source.place: Internal sheaf Hom on opens; algebra.tex Tag 0311 applied in Step 8.

proof.text:
For every open $U$ and $s\in F(U)$ define a morphism $F^\dagger|_U\to\omega_C|_U$ by sending $\varphi\in F^\dagger(T)$ to $\varphi_T(s|_T)$ on every $T\subseteq U$. It is linear in $\varphi$ and $s$ and respects restrictions, since local module morphisms do. By [def-pur-sheaf-hom] these maps define $\delta_F:F\to F^{\dagger\dagger}$. Equality of all such section values forces equality of the morphisms, proving uniqueness. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-internal-hom-finite-presentation] twice shows that at every $x$ its map is exactly
$$M\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_A(\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,W),W),\qquad m\longmapsto(\phi\longmapsto\phi(m)),$$
where $A=\mathcal O_{C,x}$, $M=F_x$, and $W=(\omega_C)_x$.

source.place: Tag 0B5A (lemma-local-CM), canonical evaluation morphism, expressed via local sheaf Hom.

proof.text: Let $x$ be closed, with $A,M,W$ as in Step 10. By Step 4, $K_x\cong W[1]$ is a normalized algebraic dualizing complex over the Noetherian local ring $A$. If $M=0$, both ordinary Hom duals vanish and $\delta_{F,x}$ is already an isomorphism. Suppose $M\ne0$. Its depth is one by Step 7, and its support dimension $d_M$ is at most one. Apply [lem-sfb-normalized-dualizing-depth-detection] to $M,K_x$. Clause (1) kills $E^j=H^j(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M[0],K_x))$ for $j<-1$ and $j>0$, and clause (2), using depth one, kills $E^0$. Consequently this derived Hom is concentrated in degree $-1$.

Put $N=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,W)$. By [lem-pur-derived-internal-hom-shift-comparison] and [lem-sc-rhom-cohomology-ext-ring] at $n=0$, followed by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful],
$$E^{-1}=H^0(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M[0],W[0]))=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,W)=N.$$
Together with Step 11 and [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] this identifies $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M[0],K_x)$ with $N[1]$ in $D(A)$. This is concentration of the whole derived object, not an assertion of degreewise isomorphisms alone. Choose this isomorphism to induce the displayed identification on degree-minus-one cohomology, adjusting by an automorphism of N if necessary.

Apply [lem-trf-finite-module-canonical-biduality] to the finite $A$-module $M$ and $L=K_x$; both bounded-injective representability and the scalar-action isomorphism hold by Step 4. It gives the canonical isomorphism
$$M[0]\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M[0],K_x),K_x)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(N[1],W[1])\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(N[0],W[0]).$$
The last comparison is [lem-pur-derived-internal-hom-shift-comparison] with $m=n=1$. Its degree-zero cohomology is $\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,W)$ by [lem-sc-rhom-cohomology-ext-ring] and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful]. The canonical-biduality statement specifies evaluation on Hom representatives. Thus the induced map is evaluation $m\mapsto(\phi\mapsto\phi(m))$: in the two shifted degree-$-1$ slots it evaluates $\phi$ on the degree-zero $m$, so the graded interchange contributes $(-1)^{0\cdot(-1)}=1$. The Hom differential and shift comparisons are those of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Hence the very map $\delta_{F,x}$ of Step 10 is an isomorphism, not just a module map between abstractly isomorphic objects.

source.place: Tag 0B5A (lemma-local-CM), biduality in its proof; Tag 0A7C (lemma-dualizing), canonical evaluation comparison.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth], the kernel and cokernel of $\delta_F$ are coherent. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact], their closed-point stalks vanish, using Steps 11--13. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] their supports are closed; the same quasi-compact Kolmogorov argument of Step 3, using [lem-sc-scheme-sober, lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point], makes both supports empty. Their sections therefore vanish, since a section with every germ zero is locally zero and the sheaf axiom glues those zeros. Thus kernel and cokernel are zero and $\delta_F$ is an isomorphism. Coherence and detection of $F^\dagger$ were proved in Steps 5 and 9. This also covers $F=0$, components where its generic rank is zero, and disconnected curves.

source.place: Sheaf form of dualizing.tex Tag 0B5A, with closed-support detection on the proper curve.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0B5A (lemma-local-CM), proof, using existing 0A7U depth bounds and 0A7C canonical biduality; curves.tex Tags 0BS2/0BS3 for the dualizing sheaf realization. Associated-prime arguments are written out from algebra.tex Tags 058A, 00LL and 0311.
